industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence moved towards the tape. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): third-quarter beats were sold (Sandvik down 5%, Atlas Copco down 8%, Hiab down 12%), Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) says 'a lot is priced in' with the order strength coming from data centres the market no longer pays for, and the exception is the non-AI compounder (Hexagon, 13% organic growth); against it, offshore services and nuclear have multi-year visibility and electrical equipment is still the physical bottleneck. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment, Diversified groups, Distributors, Test and measurement and Engineered components at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Five live holdings (19.35 points of the book) sit here, judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: a tape that sells beats is a regime statement; for B: the order data remain the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack. To D on a second week of beats sold with relative strength falling to F.

sector.key: O.13. Renewable energy equipment and installation
sector.why: Neutral, from Underweight, because the condition written on the row last week fired: 'back to C if relative strength is B or better in the next reading'; Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, A prior, with the 16-Oct-26 reading at D. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the regime is still against debt-funded, long-duration capital spending with the Fed hiking in December, and the energy transition was not spoken to by any source (the thematics report lists it as unspoken), which is why this is Neutral and not Overweight; for it, the first bond rally of the cycle (Goldman upgrading bonds to overweight) is the first sign of the yields cap that rate-sensitive capital spending needs, and the tape has turned. One Pool name, SMA Solar (Sell-side Momentum A, Technical Momentum D, TSR/Valuation A), whose Thematic Fit/Momentum is recomputed on this letter. Counter-case: a rank-based grade that went A to D to B inside two months is as likely noise as signal, and nothing in the regime changed for this group; back to D if the next reading is D or the Fed path is marked up further.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Germany this week (a source pack is present, 2026-W43, and it carried nothing country-specific here), relative strength is not graded by country, and Richard's view is G10 and Europe-wide with no country line. An absence is an absence; no tilt.
